data.title: Middle East Eye: Pezeshkian says Iran no longer trusts negotiations with the US
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Pezeshkian says Iran no longer trusts negotiations with the US
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has told Al Jazeera that Iran no longer trusts negotiations with the United States after previous rounds of talks were followed by attacks and sanctions.
"The day after the US president's speech, it was our turn to speak. In effect, he threatened to wipe Iran off the map and labelled us as 'terrorist'," he said.
"This is the fourth or fifth time we have held talks. What has happened, and continues to happen is that we no longer trust these talks. No matter how much we negotiate, after a while they start attacking us, imposing sanctions and taking the kinds of actions they have taken before."
"At least we have reached an understanding on a framework and announced it. Now the Americans have to respond. Are they willing to move within this framework, or do they want to derail the process again?" the president said.
Pezeshkian told Al Jazeera that previous rounds of talks were followed by attacks and sanctions (AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel's attorney general orders postponement of E1 settlement tender
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israel's attorney general orders postponement of E1 settlement tender
Israel’s attorney general has ordered a one-month postponement of an E1 settlement construction tender in the West Bank to avoid it being used for electioneering, Al Jazeera reported.
The tender, published on 18 August, covers seven residential compounds containing 1,234 housing units, out of the 3,401 units approved for E1, according to Israeli media. The deadline for bids had been set for 19 October, eight days before the Knesset election.
E1 (East 1) would link Ma’ale Adumim and other illegal Israeli settlements to occupied East Jerusalem, effectively severing the West Bank and disrupting Palestinian movement between the northern and southern West Bank, and isolating communities on each side.
The European Union has said the E1 settlement project fundamentally undermines the prospects for a two-state solution.
It noted that these developments come amid increasing instability in the West Bank and record levels of settler violence.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Saudi Arabia calls for 'comprehensive' regional navigation security
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Saudi Arabia calls for 'comprehensive' regional navigation security
Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan used his address at the UN General Assembly to call for serious international cooperation to protect freedom of navigation and stress that a regional security framework should be "comprehensive".
“Protecting international navigation is a shared responsibility that requires serious international cooperation,” he said.
Prince Faisal, who led the Saudi delegation at the UNGA, added that Riyadh supports efforts to reduce tensions in the region and stressed that "any arrangements for its security be comprehensive".
He also supported initiatives aimed at de-escalation, particularly efforts by Qatar and Pakistan, saying they can help restore regional stability.
The minister accused Iran of flagrant attacks on civilian and economic targets across the region, while calling on the international community to condemn Houthi actions threatening Red Sea shipping.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US thanks Turkey, Oman, UAE for supporting sanctions against Iran
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US thanks Turkey, Oman, UAE for supporting sanctions against Iran
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has thanked the governments of the United Kingdom, Turkey, Oman and the UAE for supporting Washington’s "Operation Economic Outcast", a harsh economic campaign against Iran.
"At my direction, teams were dispatched across the globe to engage with countries and demand action against the Iranian regime," he said on X.
“These efforts are delivering results,” he wrote.
Bessent noted that Turkey and Oman have halted incoming flights from private carrier Mahan Air, while the United Arab Emirates has stopped all flights by Iranian airlines.
Dubai, the UAE's commercial hub, is a major destination for Iran's carriers, with multiple daily flights, a large Iranian community and close business links. Bessent also highlighted new banking restrictions.
On Wednesday, the UAE central bank blocked transactions to and from Iran by branches of Iran's Bank Melli, accusing it of violating laws on money laundering, terrorism and arms proliferation.
Last week, Turkey revoked the license of Iran's Bank Mellat, a semi-private financial entity that has been subject to Western sanctions for years.
“I appreciate the governments of the UK, Turkiye, Oman, and the UAE. We will continue working together as there is more to be done to prevent Tehran from carrying out its terrorist agenda,” Bessent wrote.
Following the launch of Operation Economic Outcast, @USTreasury imposed targeted financial measures against banks and aviation service providers. At my direction, teams were dispatched across the globe to engage with countries and demand action against the Iranian regime.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Three Palestinians injured in Israeli drone attacks on Gaza
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Three Palestinians injured in Israeli drone attacks on Gaza
Two Palestinians were injured, one critically, on Sunday morning after an Israeli drone targeted a group of Palestinians in Al-Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, Wafa reported.
Another Palestinian was injured when an Israeli drone struck near tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the vicinity of Sheikh Radwan Market, north of Gaza City.
The report said that Israeli forces also shelled areas south of Khan Younis and opened fire from military vehicles east of the city. At the same time, artillery shelling and heavy gunfire targeted the Mawasi Rafah area in the southern Gaza Strip.
Israeli military helicopters also opened heavy fire east of Gaza City, while tanks and naval vessels fired toward the northwestern areas of the city, according to Wafa.
In the occupied West Bank, meanwhile, Wafa reported that Israeli forces tightened restrictions by closing the gate at the entrance to the town of Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah, and “harassed citizens”.
They also closed the entrances to villages such as Aboud, Nabi Saleh, Atara and Taybeh and set up a military checkpoint at the entrance to Yabroud and Ein Sinya, the report said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iraq seeks US exemption from sanctions on Iranian airlines
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Iraq seeks US exemption from sanctions on Iranian airlines
The Iraqi government has said it is in talks with the United States to seek an exemption from sanctions on Iranian airlines, which have disrupted travel for patients, students and pilgrims.
All Iraqi airports enforced the US ban this week, resulting in major disruption at the airport serving the holy city of Najaf, the main destination in Iraq for Iranian flights.
"The Iraqi government is holding direct talks with the American side to exempt certain Iraqi airports from these measures," the prime minister's media office said.
An exemption, it added, would allow flights to resume "for humanitarian reasons, including medical treatment, education, religious visits, and for the interest of civilians".
Iranian airlines mainly carry Iraqi Shia pilgrims to Iran's holy cities or Iranians visiting sacred sites in Iraq. The flights also serve Iraqi students studying in Iran and patients seeking medical treatment there.
In an interview with Iranian news agency ISNA, Iran's ambassador to Iraq Mohammad Kazem Al-Sadegh said his country was also in contact with authorities in Baghdad to find a way to restore the flights.
"There are roughly 25 daily flights from Iran to Najaf and about 15 flights to Baghdad, and... around 12,000 to 13,000 people travel between Iran and Iraq and vice versa on Iranian airlines, which is not a small number," he said.
Report by AFP

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has called on Israel to “go to war” in the occupied West Bank and “do what we did in Gaza”.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports
Parents across Riyadh received emails from schools on Sunday announcing a last-minute plan to shift to remote learning for a week, according to messages seen by AFP.
"We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week," read two separate messages seen by AFP.
There was no official reason given but the move comes amid heightened tensions in the Gulf and near-daily attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia by the Houthi fighters in Yemen.
"When a decision affects an entire school community for a full week, families deserve clear communication and transparency about the reasons behind it," one parent living in Riyadh who spoke on condition of anonymity told AFP.
"It's a last-minute decision. We have no clue what's happening," a Lebanese expatriate living in Riyadh added.
The announcement comes a day after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom.
The strikes were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war.
The United Nations Security Council earlier condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi fighters, noting that the strikes have wounded "civilians, including women and children".
Report by AFP

data.title: Middle East Eye: US ships in Indian Ocean will be hit if US launches new attacks, IRGC says
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US ships in Indian Ocean will be hit if US launches new attacks, IRGC says
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has warned it will attack US warships, even those in the Indian Ocean, if Washington launches new attacks against Iran, Iranian media reported.
“If Trump considers the Strait of Hormuz his strait, then why aren’t his ships and vessels here?” Ali Mohammadi, the IRGC Navy’s deputy for political affairs, said, according to the Fars news agency.
On Saturday, Trump posted an image on his Truth Social platform showing the Strait of Hormuz circled and labelled “Trump Strait”, hours after Iran said it had presented a seven-day plan to reopen the strategic waterway.
Mohammadi said the US “should just bring one of its ships close to this area” if it claims to control the waterway.
“If another war breaks out, we will undoubtedly attack and hit their ships and destroyers even in the Indian Ocean,” he warned.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Protesters march on Labour conference, call for ending arms sales to Israel
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Protesters march on Labour conference, call for ending arms sales to Israel
Hundreds of pro-Palestine protesters marched on Labour’s annual conference, the first after Andy Burnham took over as prime minister, in Liverpool and called for an end to UK arms sales to Israel.
Some of the protesters called for expanding the sanctions, which were imposed by the UK government recently on West Bank settlements, to all of Israel.
Britain has announced the country's strongest package of sanctions against Israel’s illegal settlements, targeting the trade, finance and services that sustain their expansion across the occupied West Bank.
In September 2024, the newly elected Starmer government suspended around 30 export licences for UK-made arms after assessing there was a "clear risk" the items could be used in Gaza in serious violations of international humanitarian law.
But the same government also approved $169m worth of military equipment for Israel over the next three months.
Protesters have called for wider sanctions against Israel (AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: US-led coalition to withdraw from Iraqi Kurdistan by 30 September
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
US-led coalition to withdraw from Iraqi Kurdistan by 30 September
US-led coalition forces are scheduled to withdraw from facilities in Iraq's Kurdistan region by 30 September under an agreement between Baghdad and Washington to wind down the coalition mission.
The move follows a series of military base handovers to Iraqi forces since 2025 and marks a key step in Iraq's transition to bilateral security arrangements with the United States.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi told the United Nations General Assembly on Friday that the end of the international coalition's mission would move Iraq's relationship with its strategic partners from military cooperation to economic and development cooperation.
Zaidi urged all countries to tighten border controls, close gaps and remain vigilant against conditions that fuel extremism.
Report by Reuters

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli police 'reopen' probe into pepper-spray attack on Armenian boy
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israeli police 'reopen' probe into pepper-spray attack on Armenian boy
Israeli police have reopened an investigation into the pepper-spraying of a nine-year-old Armenian Christian boy in Jerusalem, after closing it despite the assault being captured on security cameras, according to Israeli journalist Yossi Eli.
"Following my expose and the shock from what happened to William, the police have reopened the case and will collect the cameras. If this weren't so sad, it would be gratifying that the police only work like this," Eli wrote on X.
The boy, identified only as William, was riding his bicycle near the Mamilla neighbourhood on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, while listening to music through headphones.
A group of men approached him and demanded he remove his headphones, which he did. After hearing him speak English, one of the men said, "No English, Jews," before spraying him with pepper spray.
A video shared by Eli shows William seen crying inside an ambulance as his mother reassures him that his younger sister, Arev, is safe.
Eli reported that this was the second attack on William. In the first, he was accompanied by his father, who intervened to protect him; this time, he was alone.

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'I'm a man of strong faith,' says Irish goalkeeper after withdrawing from Israel match
data.author: Qazi Zaid
data.summary:
'I'm a man of strong faith,' says Irish goalkeeper after withdrawing from Israel match
Republic of Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu has withdrawn from the team’s Nations League match against Israel, saying his decision was based on his opposition to the killing of civilians.
“My decision is based purely on the belief the killing of innocent people is wrong,” Bazunu said in a statement posted on social media.
“Representing my country means everything to me,” Bazunu wrote. “I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of morals and principles, therefore I feel that participating in the upcoming matches against Israel would be wrong.”
He added: “There are times when you have the opportunity to stand for a greater cause, and I strongly believe this is one of those moments.”
The Republic of Ireland will nevertheless play Israel in Sunday's Uefa Nations League match in Debrecen, Hungary, after the squad voted by a significant majority to proceed with the fixture, Football Association of Ireland CEO David Courell said on Saturday.
The vote followed several hours of discussions at the team hotel over whether to boycott the game.
Ireland will wear black armbands during the match and will not shake hands with the Israeli players before kickoff, according to the report.

Submitted by

Jewish visitors pray at an entrance to the Al-Aqsa Mosque during Tisha B’Av in Jerusalem’s Old City, 23 July 2026 (Ammar Awad/Reuters)

Hamas political bureau member Khaled Meshaal has warned that Israeli actions and measures around Al-Aqsa Mosque are “paving the way for total control and domination over the site”.
Meshaal said the measures included the reported 40-day closure of the mosque, what he described as the “imposition of temporal division” to facilitate incursions by “extremist Jewish groups” and efforts to create “spatial division” by emptying key facilities within the courtyard, according to a statement.
Al-Aqsa “stands at a crossroads”, Meshaal said, and called for steps to protect the site, including what he called a “strategy of resistance and jihad”.
He also urged Arab and Muslim-majority countries to back Palestine and called on Palestinians to keep a “steadfast presence” at the mosque.
The comments come a week after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu toured tunnels beneath Al-Aqsa Mosque as hundreds of Israeli settlers raided the Jerusalem holy site.
Netanyahu joined tens of thousands of Israelis for Selichot prayers at the Western Wall, adjacent to Al-Aqsa, ahead of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
The prime minister later posted a video of himself and his wife, Sara, touring tunnels beneath the Al-Aqsa Mosque complex.
“It is moving to touch the rock of our existence. We are here very close to the Holy of Holies,” he said. “We are here, and we will always remain here.”
On 20 September, hundreds of Israelis raided Al-Aqsa, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'Comprehensive closure': Israel to shut down all West Bank crossings, Wafa reports
data.author: Qazi Zaid
data.summary:
'Comprehensive closure': Israel to shut down all West Bank crossings, Wafa reports
Israeli forces have tightened restrictions around the occupied West Bank city of Ramallah, closing roads and entrances to several towns and villages, Wafa news agency reported.
The development comes after Israeli authorities decided to impose a “comprehensive closure” on the occupied West Bank and close crossings into the territory until Saturday for the Jewish holiday of Sukkot.
Local sources told the agency that the entrance gate to Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah, was closed and residents were “harassed”.
Wafa also reported that entrances to Aboud, Nabi Saleh, Atara and Taybeh were closed, while military checkpoints were set up at the entrances to Yabroud and Ein Sinyah.
